page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this KVM-hypervised instance provides a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, allocating 8.0 GB of memory per physical core. The processor features a 35 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, which assist in vector calculations and deep learning inference workloads. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, alongside poor single-threaded gzip compression speeds. However, the instance leverages its 32 dedicated cores to deliver average multi-core performance. Multi-threaded benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, consistently rank in the middle 50% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth also performs at an average level, with uncached large-block read speeds reaching 99.19 GB/sec and write speeds at 49.44 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1ne.8xlarge offers a dense memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads that require large memory footprints but do not demand top-tier single-thread CPU speeds. The trade-off lies in its moderate processing clock speed and lack of local NVMe storage, which requires careful planning for disk-I/O intensive tasks. This hardware profile is well-suited for memory-intensive applications such as relational databases, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded data processing tasks.
